[41~42] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.

Violence has harmful effects on human beings of any culture, geographic area, or social class. There is abundant literature on the effects of traumatic events and disasters on human beings. As expected, terrorist attacks have important psychological effects on the direct victims, which, moreover, seem long-lasting.
But what about the general population, which is the end target of terrorist attacks? The existing data offer a very (a) different panorama from that of direct victims. Despite the frequently alarmist discourse of the political and academic authorities, the data show that the impact is usually much more (b) significant than would be expected. Despite numerous initial reactions of moderate or high stress in the general population, most of the studies have failed to (c) reveal high rates of posttraumatic stress disorder(PTSD), or concomitant increases in the use of mental health services and psychotropics.
In fact, the pattern of the general population is more often one of resilience than of (d) vulnerability to terrorist acts. Resilience has been defined as "the ability to maintain a relatively stable, healthy level of psychological functioning" in the face of highly adverse events or "the adult capacity to maintain healthy, symptom-free functioning". Although resilience to trauma has conventionally been thought to be rare, only emerging in psychologically exceptional individuals, the data show that most people who face potentially traumatic situations react without (e) showing signs of major mental disorders. Many people display no psychological effects, not even short-lived ones.

* concomitant: 동시에 일어나는 ** resilience: 회복력

[43~45] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.

(A)
James recently discovered that his son Leo had developed a new hobby. Leo spent every night watching the stars and taking notes, and James was wondering how he could best support his son's new passion. Then, James thought of his old friend Lucas, who worked at an observatory, and called him. When James told him about his son, Lucas showed interest and said, "Why don't you bring (a) him to the observatory? It would be great for Leo to properly experience what he enjoys."

(B)
Using the large telescope, Lucas observed the Milky Way with Leo. Leo was left breathless by the brightness and size of the stars (b) he saw through the telescope for the first time. Lucas explained the names, locations, and characteristics of the stars, and Leo took notes eagerly while listening. The moment he realized that the stars he watched every night weren't just shining dots, but stars with their own names and stories, Leo felt deeply moved. It was James's first time seeing (c) his son so focused and happy.

(C)
After the tour, Lucas gave Leo a small star map and said, "This is a gift for you. From now on, (d) you'll be able to find and record the names of stars at home." Leo was delighted and thankful, and James also came to understand his son's hobby in a new way. After that, Leo observed the stars and kept records every night. His room became filled with star maps and notebooks. Looking at his son, James was proud of Leo's passion for the night sky.

(D)
A few days later, James and Leo headed to the observatory where Lucas worked. As soon as they arrived, Leo saw an enormous telescope, with his eyes sparkling and his mouth wide open. Looking at Leo with a warm smile, Lucas asked, "Leo, you really love the stars in the sky, don't you? Would you like to observe the stars in more detail with (e) me today?" Leo replied in an excited voice, "Yes! I had so many questions looking at the sky every night!"

20. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

With thousands of articles published every year there is a lot of competition for the limited time that most people have for reading. The Abstract is by far the most important part of any scientific article. Only a minority of readers will read beyond the Abstract, so this must contain the key messages you want to convey in your paper. Usually this is done by summarizing each of the major parts of the paper — Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion — in one to four sentences each, essentially a micro-version of the paper. Choose your words carefully because electronic searches of journal articles are usually based on words in the title and abstract. These search engines often provide the Abstract of a paper to readers, another reason why it must present your critical information.
* abstract: 초록(抄錄)
choices: 초록에는 논문의 핵심 메시지와 주요 정보가 제시되어야 한다.

21. 밑줄 친 technology is not magic이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

There is not always a technological fix even for problems that are mainly technological. In the real world, there are limits, tradeoffs, and impossibilities. Often enough, the technology that solves one problem creates others. As hard as it may be to believe today, in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the automobile was promoted in part as a technological fix for urban pollution. Horse-drawn transport had polluted the cities with an accumulation of animal waste that threatened public health. The automobile neatly solved that problem. Yet today, automobiles are one of the largest single sources of health-threatening urban air pollution, noise, and greenhouse gas emissions. History certainly has its ironies. The fact is, technology is not magic. It is the result of a systematic creative process of thinking and experimentation carried out by fallible human beings who inescapably embed the essential imperfection that makes them human into every technology they develop. Not only does every particular technology have its own limits, technology itself is limited in what it can be expected to accomplish.
choices: the development of technology results in unsustainable costs
technological solutions can lead to unintended new problems
resources are bound to be wasted in the development of technology
the number of jobs available decreases as technology advances

22. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

In common usage, “national security” refers to the protection of the nation-state. But when you think about it, it is not the security of the nation-state as such that is fundamental; it is the security of the individual. Nations are, after all, artificial constructs that have been created by real human beings in pursuit of objectives that seemed more attainable collectively than individually. Security is certainly among the most important of those objectives. In short, people do not exist to protect nations; nations exist to protect people. Nations are abstractions; people are not. Groups are a critical intermediary between the individual and the huge collection of individuals that make up the nation-state. Group identities and norms have considerable impact on the lives of individuals. Still, personal security is the most basic concept. National security is relevant only to the extent that maintaining the integrity of the state is an effective way of maintaining the security and well-being of the people who live within its jurisdiction.

* integrity: 온전함 ** jurisdiction: 관할권

23. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]

The term autobiography remains the most widely used and most generally understood term for life narrative. But because the term privileges the autonomous individual and the universalizing life story as the definitive achievement of life writing, it has been vigorously challenged in the wake of poststructuralist, postmodern, and postcolonial critiques of the Enlightenment subject. Early twentieth-century theorists acclaimed this master narrative of “the sovereign self” as an institution of literature and culture, and identified a canon of representative self-life-writings. Implicit in this canonization, however, was the assumption that many other kinds of life writings produced at the same time had lesser value and were not “true” autobiography — “slave” narrative, narratives of women’s domestic lives, coming-of-age and travel narratives, among them. Thus, many postmodern and postcolonial theorists contend that the term autobiography is inadequate to describe the extensive historical range and the diverse genres and practices of life writing around the globe.

* sovereign: 자주적인 ** canon: 정전(기본적 중요 문헌)
choices: clarity of the meaning conveyed by the term autobiography
necessity of canonizing traditional autobiographies in literature
reasons for the exclusion of autobiography from narrative writing

problems.text:
24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

As the twentieth century came to an end, leaders were confident that they knew what they were doing, that steadily increasing prosperity was a sensible and achievable shared goal. In the United States, economists spoke of the “great moderation”; in the United Kingdom, politicians celebrated the “end of boom and bust.” The idea that sustained growth could be achieved through modest interventions was taken for granted. And our apparent success created the impression that an expanding economy was the norm, with any slowdown to be regarded as an unfortunate but temporary exception. Today, that assuredness feels misplaced. Almost every country has slumped its way into the twenty-first century, though the timing differs: Japan and Germany started struggling in the mid-1990s, the US and UK in the mid-2000s, China in the 2010s. Most economies, weakened by two decades of crises — including the dot-com bust, the 2007-2008 financial crisis, and the Covid-19 pandemic — are a weak shadow of former selves. We increasingly realize we cannot take growth for granted.
choices: Why Economic Slumps Are the Key to Future Stability
Basis for a Return to Rapid Growth in the 21st Century
The End of Optimism: Economic Growth No Longer Guaranteed
Learning from the Past: How to Predict the Next Economic Bust
The Golden Rule of Economics: Growth Is Always the Norm!

26. Herbert Simon에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Born on June 15, 1916, in Milwaukee, U.S., Herbert Simon was an American scholar whose work influenced the fields of computer science, economics, and cognitive psychology. In 1933, Simon entered the University of Chicago and decided to study social science and mathematics. He was interested in studying biology but chose not to pursue it as his major because of his color-blindness and awkwardness in the laboratory. Simon was a pioneer in artificial intelligence. With Allen Newell, he developed a production-rule theory of human problem-solving and won the ACM Turing Award in 1975. Simon has been credited with revolutionary changes in microeconomics. He is the one who created the concept of organizational decision-making as it is known today, and it was in this area that he was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1978. Simon lived a life marked by wide-ranging interests, from the arts to mountain climbing, and died in 2001 at the age of 84.

인공지능 분야의 선구자였다.
1978년에 노벨상을 받았다.
예술부터 등산까지 여러 분야에 관심이 많았다.

33. Guppies are quite variably colored fish and a number of studies have shown that females prefer males with more orange. Dugatkin conducted a simple experiment that quickly became a standard for animal mate choice studies. A focal female was placed in an aquarium in which there was a male on each side separated from the focal female by a pane of glass. The female could freely move within the aquarium and be courted by each male on the other side of the glass divider. The focal female spent more time courting the male with more orange. The focal female was then moved back to the middle of the aquarium and constrained inside a glass cylinder. A live "model" female guppy was placed with the less preferred male and the focal female could observe the two interacting. The model female was removed, the choice test was repeated, and the focal female now switched her preference to the previously less preferred male. The interpretation was that _______________ once he was observed courting another female. [3점]
* focal: (실험에서) 대상이 되는 ** court: 구애하다
choices: the male’s physical orange color faded
the more preferred male became more aggressive
the perceived attractiveness of the male increased
the male’s ability to distinguish colors improved
the male simply got bored with the courting activities

Whether or not the phrase ‘no one’s land’ was in use (a controversial question), the assumption behind it was certainly current among white settlers from the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries. Like Columbus, when he took possession of ‘the Indies’ in 1492, British colonists did not want to know about the use of the land before their arrival, by the First Peoples in the Americas, the Maori in New Zealand and Aboriginal groups in Australia. Some people bring threats and disease, but they are also the source of the most important benefits in our lives. To be evolutionarily successful, our ancient ancestors needed to get along with other folks. ① Anthropologists who study hunter-gatherer groups (of the sort our ancestors evolved in) have found that making friends and forming alliances are essential to evolutionary success. ② For example, anthropologists Kim Hill and Magdalena Hurtado went deep into the rain forests of South America to study a group called the Aché, carefully recording which members of the tribe shared food with one another. ③ They found that in such groups friends provide a natural insurance policy against starvation. ④ The follow-up study revealed that building friendship led to increased competition for resources within groups, which could threaten the overall stability essential for survival. ⑤ Without refrigeration, one family cannot eat a whole pig, but a group of families sharing their catches can pool their risk and stand a better chance of making it through tough times.

38.
Similarly, instant messaging is psychologically more real than corresponding by email.

Interactivity is a crucial element in the psychological reality of cyberspace. The greater and the more profound the interaction is, the greater degree of psychological reality we attach to it. ( ① ) Thus, psychological reality is perceived to be greater if what we send and what we receive consist not merely of words that we type, but also of voices, pictures, and body movements. ( ② ) The outputs we send are of greater psychological reality for us the more their execution seems natural to us; for example, the less effort we need to control them. ( ③ ) The psychological reality of the inputs we receive is determined by features such as the speed and frequency of the responses that express the sender's psychological attitude toward us. ( ④ ) An immediate response is psychologically more exciting, just as live broadcasting is more exciting. ( ⑤ ) The more similar the inputs and outputs are to offline interaction, the more real they are typically perceived to be. [3점]

39.
Plants benefit from the presence of animals in some fundamental, if inconspicuous, ways.

It is common to think of plants as suffering from the attentions of animals. First and foremost, plants are food for animals; with minor exceptions like carnivorous plants and some microorganisms, they are always the first link in a food chain. ( ① ) Because essentially all the biomass of a forest is in the plants, they comprise the physical habitat for many animals. ( ② ) Soil invertebrates and some other creatures may not need living plants in which to hide or seek shelter from harsh weather, but most forest animals would be very exposed without a cover of vegetation. ( ③ ) They use the carbon dioxide that animals exhale and the nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus, that animals help make available through their participation in the decomposition of plant matter. ( ④ ) Plants also benefit from a special feature of animals, the ability to move. ( ⑤ ) Many plant species have evolved ways to exploit this ability in order to move pollen from plant to plant and to disperse seeds away from their parents.

* inconspicuous: 눈에 잘 띄지 않는 ** invertebrate: 무척추동물

40. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

When we conform, it is not so much the power of the group or peer pressure that shapes our behavior, but rather our desire to be accepted. Our need to conform is a powerful force that shapes us and literally changes the way we think. In other words, it is not just public compliance when we conform to the group but true private acceptance of group norms. For example, when asked to rate the attractiveness of music or faces, if there is a difference between an individual's liking and the group consensus, this triggers activation in brain regions associated with social cognition and reward evaluation. However, as soon as we have an ally on our side, we become more self-opinionated. In Asch's test, it only required the presence of one other dissenter against the group for the effect to reduce significantly. When we are accompanied by another dissenter, we are no longer an individual but part of a new group.

* ally: 동조자 ** dissenter: 반대자
↓
Our need for acceptance drives group conformity and can (A) our mindset, yet having just one person who disagrees with the group consensus (B) this influence, letting us stand our ground.
choices: reinforce …… extends
alter …… weakens
hide …… maintains
express …… neutralizes
reshape …… strengthens
